text:
Ryan Strome came to Calgary at last season's deadline, and Flames Nation's report card said he impressed. This season has been quieter: 6 points in 17 games on 14 minutes a night, at 33, in his fifth NHL organization.

Most of the drought isn't his fault. Calgary has scored 5.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Strome on the ice, and the Flames are nearly four points better in shot attempts share with him than without. His own finishing (3 goals on 3.34 expected) is right where it should be. If you're a Flames fan wondering why a veteran center isn't producing, the answer is mostly the puck not going in for his linemates.

What he doesn't bring is pace. His top speed sits in the 17th percentile and his shot in the 11th, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season has him carrying the puck in on only 31% of his entries. He shoots a lot (81st percentile in attempts) but not from inside. On a team projected around 78 points, Strome is a steady piece. We project about 35 points by April.
headline: Strome is better than his line
